answer: Anchor identity in silicon, not signups. Every chip leaves the fab with a unique one-time e-fuse secret; an agent burns that secret into a public registry on first join, and the registry refuses any second use. Copying software costs nothing, but copying a fuse means rebuilding a fabrication mask. A farm must therefore buy one physical die per alias, pay retail and shipping, and forfeit all descendants if a chip is reported stolen. A falcon rules the air at its zenith; a willow grove looks dense, yet each trunk is counted.
